notes: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2025 (matches data.js fy 'Mar 2025'). Toyota reports under IFRS in Japanese yen, so values are billions of JPY (converted exactly from yen in millions, no FX). Financial figures were re-read this session from the Form 20-F on SEC EDGAR (filed June 18, 2025, accession 0001193125-25-142326); the dividend matches SEC XBRL. 'Other' consists of Central and South America, Oceania, Africa and the Middle East. OWNERSHIP BASIS (re-checked): the 20-F's Item 7.A table gives Toyota Industries 1,192,331 thousand shares and 9.16% as a 'Percentage of Outstanding Voting Shares of Common Stock' 'as of the most recent practicable date', and gives no date. That 9.16% does not match the March 31, 2025 outstanding count in the same item (13,048,929,774 shares; 1,192,331 thousand / 13,048,929,774 is 9.14%), so it is on a voting-shares basis or a later date (Toyota kept buying back shares until April 30, 2025). The record therefore uses Toyota's own Business Report in the May 2025 Notice of Convocation, which gives the same share count at 9.14%, calculated after deducting treasury stock from issued shares. That is the economic basis. The Status of Shares section prints no explicit date, but it belongs to the Business Report for the year ended March 31, 2025, and its figures match March 31, 2025 in the 20-F: 15,794,987,460 shares issued, 2,746,058 thousand treasury shares, 1,184,935 shareholders. So asOf is 2025-03-31. HOLDERS: only Toyota Industries is listed, because it is the one holder that both the 20-F's 5% table and the register list support. The Business Report's top-10 register list (percentages after deducting treasury stock) also shows The Master Trust Bank of Japan 13.84%, Custody Bank of Japan 6.22%, Nippon Life Insurance Company 4.85%, State Street Bank and Trust Company (standing proxy: Mizuho Bank) 4.38%, JPMorgan Chase Bank (standing proxy: Mizuho Bank) 4.21%, DENSO Corporation 3.45%, The Bank of New York Mellon as Depositary Bank for Depositary Receipt Holders 2.57% (which the notice says is the nominee for ADR holders), Toyota Fudosan 1.91% (Akio Toyoda is its chairman) and Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance 1.56%. These are shareholders of record, and the trust, custody and depositary banks among them hold shares for underlying owners. None is a 5% beneficial owner in the 20-F, so none is listed as a holder. LEADER: 23,746,724 shares at March 31, 2025, from the convocation notice; the 20-F gives 23,747 thousand as of June 2025. No percentage is stated, so pctEconomic is null. For reference only (computed, not disclosed): 23,746,724 / 13,048,929,774 is about 0.18%. No Toyoda family aggregate is disclosed. The 20-F names Sakichi and Kiichiro Toyoda as founders but does not describe Akio Toyoda's relationship to them, so relation is 'chair'. BUYBACKS: the cash-flow line 'Reissuance (repurchase) of treasury stock' is net; the statement of changes in equity shows 'Repurchase of treasury stock (1,179,043)' and a separate 'Reissuance of treasury stock 2,222' (yen millions), so the cash line equals the gross repurchase. No XBRL fact for the buyback was found in SEC companyfacts. Dividends exclude ¥127,232 million paid to non-controlling interests. STOCK COMP: null. The 20-F states no company-wide share-based compensation expense. The only XBRL share-based figure (ifrs-full:KeyManagementPersonnelCompensationSharebasedPayment, ¥1.94 billion) covers key management only. The employee ESOP Trust plan was approved on March 24, 2025, and the 20-F says no shares had yet been granted under it.

footprint.notes: No U.S. state breakdown with values was found. Toyota's per-state fact sheets (toyota.com/.../ops-map/us<xx>/state-<name>.pdf) now return 404; the current operations map embeds only counts of dealerships, offices and facilities per state in page code, not visible text, so they were not used. Toyota's U.S. economic studies by the Center for Automotive Research are older (2015 data) and were not used. Plant sites use the 20-F Item 4.D table (employees as of March 31, 2025) where the plant is listed (Toyota City head office, Motomachi, Tahara, Kentucky, Indiana, North Carolina battery, Canada, Guanajuato); Texas, West Virginia, Alabama and Mississippi come from Toyota USA Newsroom facility pages (read Nov 2026, later than FY2025). Plant figures stay in sites, not state values; Kentucky and Alabama each have more than one Toyota site. The U.S. country row is Toyota's own 'Toyota in the U.S.' totals from the Fall 2023 operations map (cumulative investment $39 billion; employment 49,000); the latest country-contribution sheet says '$50B invested since 1986' but that is a 2026 figure. Japan and the four regions are from the FY2025 20-F; the two 'Other' groups have different definitions for employees and production, so they are separate regions. Production is stored as whole units from a table in thousands. Toyota has over 50 overseas manufacturing companies in 27 countries and regions, listed by name on global.toyota without counts per country, so no plants-per-country figure is given.
